disposition.reason: Docket 143-7-08 Vtec is the Benoits' appeal of the DRB's denial of permits to convert the main building back to four units and authorize the rear building as a residential unit. That dwelling's residential use had been enjoined, so the after-the-fact permission decides whether it may be occupied.

evidence.quote: the Benoits once again applied to the Development Review Board, this time for a permit to convert the main apartment building back to four units
a permit authorizing the use of the rear building as a residential unit
The DRB denied their application and the Benoits appealed to the Environmental Court
Judge Wright therefore enjoined further use of the rear building as a residential unit

project.description: At 53 High Street, a permit to convert the main apartment building back from five to four units, plus after-the-fact permission to use the rear building (a former nursery school, converted in 1987 without permits and later enjoined from residential use) as one residential unit; the rear unit in effect replaces the fifth main-building unit.

That matches the after-the-fact permit where occupancy is at stake. But no construction is described, and the application swaps one main-building unit for the rear unit, so the net count stays five.
See disposition; the alternative reading is a change of use without construction (no).

questions: Housing definition: the Benoits sought to convert the main building back from five to four units and legalize an existing rear dwelling whose use had been enjoined, so the net unit count is unchanged and no construction is described. Labeled housing=yes under the after-the-fact-permit-preventing-occupancy rule; confirm that this swap counts as new housing.

Should the 2021 joint motion, filed under all three captions but seeking relief from the 126-7-04 enforcement judgment, count as a reopening of this docket for duration? Counting it gives at least 4634 days; excluding it leaves the duration unknown.
